statusText:
The CME weekend halt still defines the entire horizon. NQ has not quoted since Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and will not quote again until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, about two hours beyond the end of this 24-hour window. Tail is 12% (low), the action is EA_ON and the status is green, because a pathological one-way price path cannot form while no venue is quoting.

What changed this hour is the Lebanon front, and it changed in a way that makes it materially harder to close. The strikes are now confirmed as a two-way exchange rather than a one-sided Israeli action: a Hezbollah explosive drone seriously wounded three IDF soldiers near the Ali Taher Ridge at about 02:30 local, Israel's retaliatory waves on Ansar and Deir al-Zahrani killed at least 15 including three children with 17 injured, and Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem publicly declared that 'negotiations will bring nothing but shame and disgrace'. Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam called the escalation 'extremely dangerous'. Netanyahu's spokesman still frames the strikes as intended to 'jumpstart' talks, but with Hezbollah's own leadership rejecting the table, the diplomatic off-ramp on this front has narrowed rather than widened. Stress therefore steps to 67% (high).

The hour was not one-directional, which is why the step is two points and not ten. Qatar categorically denied the circulating claim that it had detained Iranian pilots. Hamas political chief Khalil al-Hayya travelled to Cairo for talks with Egyptian officials ahead of a Jared Kushner visit to advance the Gaza plan. On the energy side, US naval forces are expanding escort capacity for vessels transiting Hormuz and additional Middle Eastern cargoes are reported heading toward depleted US inventories. Against that, an IDF tank was hit by an explosive device near the Gaza 'Yellow Line' and the military called it a grave ceasefire breach, and the Persian Gulf Strait Authority repeated that Hormuz 'remains blocked and will not be reopened until Iran's conditions are accepted'.

The hard marks are still Friday's, re-verified this hour: NQ futures 30,141.75 (-0.15%), VIX 14.25 (-2.60%), WTI $82.40 (+1.42%) and Brent $88.52 (+1.67%), with the Fed's own H.15 release confirming 2-year 4.15% and 10-year 4.63% on its latest observation. A 14-handle VIX against crude up 33% on the year remains the central unresolved divergence, and it gets resolved at the reopen, not before.
recommendation: Base strategies stay enabled: Tail 12% maps to EA_ON. There is nothing to trade into and nothing to protect against while the venue is closed - existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. Treat Sunday's 22:00 UTC restart as the single checkpoint that matters: it is the first opportunity for a full weekend of two-sided Middle East headlines, a promised Hezbollah retaliation and a scheduled US economic-isolation package to be priced at once in a thin auction, and it anchors the danger window rather than any point inside this horizon. This is general market-state analysis for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice.
headline: Weekend halt keeps Tail at 12% and status green while the Lebanon front turns into a two-way exchange and Stress steps to 67% into Sunday's 22:00 UTC restart
body:
Price path: none exists. The entire 24-hour horizon sits inside the CME weekend halt, so there is no session direction, no gap, no retracement structure, no failed pullback and no proximity to extremes to score. Every price input is a Friday close carried forward, which is the correct reason for Tail to be low and the correct reason for Confidence to sit at 66% (solid) rather than higher.

Friday's marks, re-verified from primary sources this hour: NQ futures settled 30,141.75, down 46.75 points or 0.15%, having opened at 30,210.75 against a previous close of 30,188.50 and traded a 30,028.50-30,283.00 range on 397,964 contracts, inside a 52-week span of 22,961.50-30,975.50 and up 26.6% year on year. That is a consolidation print a fraction below the highs, not a stressed tape.

Cross-asset: VIX closed 14.25, down 2.60%, in a 14.18-14.72 range and near the floor of its 13.38-35.30 52-week band - equity volatility priced for nothing to happen. On rates, the Federal Reserve's H.15 release gives 4.15% on the 2-year and 4.63% on the 10-year at its latest observation, consistent with Friday's closing marks of 4.171% and 4.696% carried by earlier runs; roughly a 50bp positive spread with no curve signal demanding attention. Crude remains the outlier: WTI $82.40 (+1.42%) and Brent $88.52 (+1.67%), up about 5% on the week, 3.5% on the month and 33% on the year, with the IEA forecasting the widest 2026 supply shortfall in five years. A 14-handle VIX alongside a 33% annual move in crude is the textbook conflicting cross-asset signal, and the contract is explicit that conflicting signals raise Stress rather than Tail.

Geopolitics is the genuinely new material this hour and it is two-sided, unlike the prior run. The Lebanon escalation is now established as an exchange rather than a one-sided action: a Hezbollah explosive drone seriously wounded three IDF soldiers near the Ali Taher Ridge around 02:30 local, and Israel's overnight and morning waves on Ansar and Deir al-Zahrani killed at least 15, including three children, with 17 injured - the deadliest sequence since the 26 June ceasefire that Hezbollah never accepted. Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem said in a televised address that 'negotiations will bring nothing but shame and disgrace'; Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam called the escalation 'extremely dangerous'; Netanyahu's spokesman insisted the strikes 'should jumpstart the talks'. A promised Hezbollah response remains outstanding. On the Iran file nothing resolved: the Persian Gulf Strait Authority repeated that Hormuz 'remains blocked and will not be reopened until Iran's conditions are accepted', the US naval blockade of Iranian ports continues, and Reuters reports 'absolutely no progress' on reviving the June interim deal. The scheduled US escalation is unchanged - Bessent's promised measures 'like the world has never seen' are still flagged for next week, with the reported menu of secondary sanctions on Chinese buyers, UAE exchange houses, asset confiscation and shadow-fleet infrastructure being explicitly oil-bullish; the exact announcement date is still unresolved between reports and is therefore deliberately not entered as a dated calendar event.

The counterweights that appeared this hour are real and are why Stress steps rather than jumps. Qatar's foreign ministry categorically denied the circulating claim that it had detained Iranian pilots. Hamas political chief Khalil al-Hayya went to Cairo for talks with Egyptian officials ahead of a Kushner visit intended to advance the Gaza plan. US naval forces are expanding escort capacity for Hormuz transits and additional Middle Eastern cargoes are reported to be heading toward depleted US inventories - both mildly supply-easing. Against them, an IDF tank was struck by an explosive device near the Gaza 'Yellow Line', which the military called a grave ceasefire breach, and the abandoned tanker Caroline Bezengi continues leaking along roughly 7.5 miles of Omani coast.

Why Tail stays at 12%: the definition requires observed persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements or NQ holding near extremes. None can be observed because nothing is quoting, and the contract forbids treating hypothetical post-event alignment as already observed. Reopening-gap risk that sits two hours beyond this horizon is not a within-horizon one-way path.

Why Stress holds high at 67%: the second front hardened into a live exchange with a retaliation explicitly promised and Hezbollah's leadership rejecting the negotiating table, the Gaza ceasefire took a fresh breach, Hormuz reopening remains foreclosed and a scheduled, oil-bullish US package is still ahead. That accumulates across a full weekend and gets repriced in a single illiquid Sunday auction against a VIX that has priced none of it. The de-escalation threads that appeared this hour cap the increment at two points; they do not justify decay.

Why Confidence is 66%: the index level, VIX, both crude benchmarks, the geopolitical thread and the full seven-day calendar were read from primary sources this hour, and the Fed's H.15 release provided an independent primary confirmation of the rates picture. Against that, the newest price evidence is now over 32 hours old with no live path to corroborate it, several domains refused the fetch (CNN, CNBC quotes, France 24, UPI - all worked around with alternative primary sources), and the date of the US sanctions announcement still cannot be resolved. Solid, not high.

Dominant mode is mixed: escalation and de-escalation threads are both live and genuinely two-sided this hour, oil and equity volatility disagree sharply, and there is no tape to arbitrate between them.

lookbackSummary: The last 24 hours contain no tradeable price action: the window opens at Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and every slot after that sits inside the CME halt. Claude published an assessment in all 24 hourly slots. Tail never left the low band, ranging 2-12%, and EA_ON green held in every slot. The informative movement is in Stress: it collapsed to 12% in the dead hours immediately after the Friday close, then climbed almost monotonically from 45% at 00:00 UTC to 65% by 20:00 UTC as weekend geopolitical headlines accumulated with no venue to price them. Confidence improved in parallel from 37% overnight to 65% as successive runs verified Friday's closes, the cross-asset picture and the seven-day calendar from primary sources. Dominant mode was mixed in every slot except the two dead hours after the close.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours are entirely inside the CME halt, so the forecast is a headline-accumulation path rather than a price path. Tail stays in the low band throughout, 12-13%, keeping EA_ON and green in every slot and drifting up only fractionally as Sunday's restart approaches. Stress holds 66-67% through Saturday evening, eases to 64% in the overnight dead zone where headline flow historically thins, then rebuilds steadily to 72% across Sunday as the reopen nears and a full weekend of Lebanon, Hormuz and US-sanctions headlines queues up for a single illiquid auction. Confidence dips to 62% overnight on pure staleness - the newest hard marks will be more than 40 hours old by then - and recovers to 68% on Sunday as Gulf shipping activity, any Hezbollah response and any statement on the promised US measures provide the first genuinely new information since Friday. The real checkpoint, the 22:00 UTC Sunday restart, sits about two hours beyond this horizon and is where the danger window is anchored.

forecastDetail.comment: The CME weekend halt owns this slot outright: NQ has not quoted since Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and does not quote again until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday. With no venue printing, persistent directional efficiency, failed pullbacks and extension are unobservable, so Tail holds at 12%. Stress steps to 67% because the Lebanon front turned into a live two-way exchange - a Hezbollah drone seriously wounded three IDF soldiers, Israel's retaliation killed 15, and Hezbollah's Qassem publicly rejected negotiating.

Still fully inside the halt. Saturday-evening headline flow is the only variable and it is running in both directions at once: escalation on the Lebanon and Gaza ceasefire lines against Qatar's denial of the Iranian-pilot story and Hamas travelling to Cairo ahead of Kushner's visit. Two-sided flow is a Stress input, not a Tail input, so Tail is unchanged at 12%.

Late Saturday in Europe, deep afternoon in the US, with no cash or futures venue open anywhere. Stress eases a point to 66% purely because the Levant news cycle historically thins after midnight Berlin, not because anything resolved - the promised Hezbollah response and the US sanctions package are both still outstanding.

Overnight dead zone begins. Confidence starts to decay on staleness alone: the newest hard marks are Friday's closes and they are now more than 36 hours old with no live tape to corroborate them. Tail stays 12% - the definitional requirements simply cannot be met without a quoting venue.

The quietest stretch of the weekend. Stress drifts to 65% as headline arrival rates fall, but it is explicitly not allowed to decay toward trivial levels while a promised Hezbollah retaliation, an unreopened Strait of Hormuz and a scheduled US economic-isolation package all sit ahead of Sunday's restart.

Sunday pre-dawn UTC. Stress bottoms near 64% and Confidence near 62%, its low for the horizon, reflecting price evidence roughly 41 hours old. From here the balance reverses: each hour closer to the 22:00 UTC restart adds reopening-gap risk to Stress while the first Gulf shipping and sanctions headlines of the new week begin to restore Confidence.
